title: Collective Dynamics of Molecular Motors
text: We study the collective dynamics of motor proteins like myosin and kinesin. In the first part we study the collective behaviour of stiffly coupled motors. We use a simple two-state model for single motors and discuss the possible funcitional forms of the resulting force-velocity relations. Then we introduce elastically coupled motors. We show that their efficiency is lowered through the flexiblity of the coupling elements. Elastically coupled motors are further shown to be able to generate waves. In the second part we study the binding of dimeric kinesin motors to microtubules in the absence of ATP. We discuss the equilibrium state as well as relaxation kinetics.
